ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p271/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p271/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p271/r1.claim: The author cites Abraham saying “peace to you,” but says this prooftext is interpreted away and does not establish that one may initiate a greeting to unbelievers.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p271/r1.anchor: وقال إبراهيم لأبيه سلام عليك وما استدل به متأول

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p271/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p271/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p271/r2.claim: The author parses nominative salāmun as a sentence and accusative salāman as a verbal noun, a prayer for safety and conciliatory address.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p271/r2.anchor: ورفع سلام على الابتداء ونصبه على المصدر، أي سلمت سلاما دعاء له بالسلامة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p271/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p271/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p271/r4.claim: The author counters permission to initiate greetings to unbelievers with the Sahih Muslim report forbidding greeting Jews and Christians first.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p271/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p271/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p271/r5.claim: Abraham's promise to ask forgiveness presupposes a condition that makes forgiveness possible, namely belief; commands and prohibitions addressed to an unbeliever likewise can be fulfilled only upon belief.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p271/r5.anchor: ثم وعده بالاستغفار وذلك يكون بشرط حصول ما يمكن معه الاستغفار وهو الإيمان بالله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p271/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p271/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p271/r6.claim: “I will ask forgiveness for you” means Abraham will pray for his father's guidance so that faith brings forgiveness; it does not mean he thought God forgives an unbeliever.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p271/r6.anchor: ومعنى سأستغفر لك أدعو الله في هدايتك فيغفر لك بالإيمان

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p271/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p271/r7.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p271/r7.claim: Ibn Atiyya allows that Abraham may have been the first prophet taught that God does not forgive unbelief; the statement to his father would then precede that revelation, later resolved by the father's death in disbelief or a revealed final judgment.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p271/r7.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون إبراهيم عليه السلام أول نبي أوحي إليه إن الله لا يغفر لكافر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p271/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p271/r8.speaker: الزمخشري، author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p271/r8.claim: Al-Zamakhshari argues that reason alone does not forbid seeking forgiveness for an unbeliever before scriptural instruction; he cites Abraham's exception and rejects the claim that the father promised to believe, arguing Abraham was the promiser, as a reading by Hammad indicates.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p271/r8.anchor: الذي يمنع من الاستغفار للكافر إنما هو السمع، فأما القضية العقلية فلا تأباه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p271/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p271/r9.speaker: ابن عباس، الكلبي، القتبي، السدي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p271/r9.claim: Ḥafiyyan means honored, gracious, and full of kindness: Ibn Abbas says compassionate, al-Kalbi forbearing, al-Qutaybi devoted, and al-Suddi one who cares about your affair.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p271/r9.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: رحيما. وقال الكلبي: حليما. وقال القتبي: بارا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p271/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p271/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p271/r10.claim: Though Abraham's father was harsh, Abraham answered with peace and a promise to seek forgiveness out of filial duty.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p271/r10.anchor: ولما كان في قوله لأرجمنك فظاظة وقساوة قلب قابله بالدعاء له بالسلام والأمن

BURSEVI:v5p259/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p259/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p259/r1.claim: Abraham’s peace is a farewell, not a prayer for kindness; it means he will not harm or insult his father, matching evil with good and permitting departure from an intractable person he advised.
BURSEVI:v5p259/r1.anchor: فهو سلام مفارقة لا سلام لطف وإحسان لأنه ليس بدعاء له

BURSEVI:v5p259/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p259/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p259/r2.claim: The future either marks what comes next or adds emphasis; Abraham asks God to enable his father’s repentance and faith.
BURSEVI:v5p259/r2.anchor: بأن يوفقك للتوبة ويهديك إلى الإيمان

BURSEVI:v5p259/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p259/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p259/r3.claim: Seeking a disbeliever’s guidance before despair of his faith is established is permissible; seeking forgiveness for one known to persist in disbelief or who dies that way is forbidden by revelation.
BURSEVI:v5p259/r3.anchor: الاستغفار بهذا المعنى للكافر قبل تبيين أنه يموت على الكفر مما لا ريب في جوازه

BURSEVI:v5p259/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p259/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p259/r4.claim: Hafiy means exceedingly kind and generous in benevolence.
BURSEVI:v5p259/r4.anchor: حفيت به بالغت وتحفيت في إكرامه بالغت

ALUSI-FULL:v16p99#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p99#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p99#2/r1.claim: “Peace be upon you” is a farewell and a way of answering evil with good: Abraham promises neither to harm nor address his father hurtfully.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p99#2/r1.anchor: توديع ومتاركة على طريقة مقابلة السيئة بالحسنة فان ترك الأساءة للمسيء إحسان

ALUSI-FULL:v16p99#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p99#2/r2.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v16p99#2/r2.claim: Another view takes the words as a greeting of farewell and allows initiating the prescribed greeting to an unbeliever, as Sufyan ibn ʿUyayna held.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p99#2/r2.anchor: تحية مفارق وجوز قائل هذا تحية الكافر

ALUSI-FULL:v16p99#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p99#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p99#2/r3.claim: Al-Alusi rejects the evidence for greeting unbelievers with salām: its proof-texts are interpreted away, and Sahih Muslim forbids initiating greeting to Jews and Christians.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p99#2/r3.anchor: وما استدل به متأول وهو محجوج بما ثبت في صحيح مسلم لا تبدءوا اليهود والنصارى بالسلام

ALUSI-FULL:v16p99#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p99#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p99#2/r4.claim: The word is read nominative as a noun or accusative as an absolute verbal noun.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p99#2/r4.anchor: بالنصب على المصدرية والرفع على الابتداء

ALUSI-FULL:v16p99#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p99#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p99#2/r5.claim: Abraham's promised forgiveness means asking God to guide his father to faith and enable repentance, as his other prayer explains.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p99#2/r5.anchor: أي استدعيه سبحانه أن يغفر لك بأن يوفقك للتوبه ويهديك إلى الأيمان

ALUSI-FULL:v16p99#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p99#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p99#2/r6.claim: Seeking guidance for a living unbeliever whose final fate is unknown is permitted; requesting it after God has revealed that the person will die in unbelief is impossible and prohibited.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p99#2/r6.anchor: مما لاريب فيه جوازه كما أنه لاريب في عدم جوازه

ALUSI-FULL:v16p99#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p99#2/r7.speaker: الطيبي
ALUSI-FULL:v16p99#2/r7.claim: Al-Tibi explains that believers were told these hostile unbelievers are God's enemies, urged to sever kinship, and then directed to Abraham as a model of estrangement, with his compassionate promise excepted because their unbelief was not yet known.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p99#2/r7.anchor: ثم بالغ جل شأنه في تفصيل عدواتهم

ALUSI-FULL:v16p100/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p100/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p100/r1.claim: The objection is that believers' prohibited prayer for unbelieving relatives, often identified as the Prophet's prayer for Abu Talib, cannot have meant asking for guidance after death—or after his unbelief was established in life.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p100/r1.anchor: أن الأستغفار الذي وقع من المؤمنين لأولى قرابتهم فنهوا عنه لأنه كان بعد التبين كان كاستغفار إبراهيم

ALUSI-FULL:v16p100/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p100/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v16p100/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says Abraham's prayer could have been conditioned on repentance and faith, and cites the report that his father promised to believe; another reading has “his father” rather than “to him.”
ALUSI-FULL:v16p100/r2.anchor: اراد اشتراط التوبة عن الكفر وقالوا آمنا

ALUSI-FULL:v16p100/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p100/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v16p100/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhshari also argues that only revelation prohibited forgiveness for unbelievers; reason alone did not, so Abraham's promise and fulfillment could have preceded the prohibition.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p100/r3.anchor: الذي منع من الأستغفار للكافر انما هو السميع فاما قضية العقل فلا تأباه

ALUSI-FULL:v16p100/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p100/r4.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v16p100/r4.claim: He argues that the exception of Abraham's promise from the command to imitate him would be pointless if the promise were merely conditional on the father's faith.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p100/r4.anchor: أنه استثنى قول إبراهيم عليه السلام

ALUSI-FULL:v16p100/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p100/r5.speaker: الكشف
ALUSI-FULL:v16p100/r5.claim: Al-Kashf records al-Razi's objection that the exception only removes the duty to imitate Abraham, not the permissibility of the act; it answers that al-Zamakhshari treats the act as not sinful for Abraham, only prohibited for later believers by revelation.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p100/r5.anchor: واعترض الأمام حديث الأستثناء بأن الآية دلت على المنع من التأسى لا أن ذلك كان معصية

ALUSI-FULL:v16p101/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p101/r1.speaker: صاحب التقريب
ALUSI-FULL:v16p101/r1.claim: The author of al-Taqrib objects that exclusion from what must be imitated proves the act is not obligatory, not that it is impermissible; he says the verse does not establish a duty to imitate.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p101/r1.anchor: واعترض صاحب التقريب بأن نفي اللازم ممنوع فان الأستثناء عما وجبت فيه الأسوة دل على أنه غير واجب

ALUSI-FULL:v16p101/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p101/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p101/r2.claim: Al-Alusi replies that the act is called objectionable and excluded from the good example, so copying it would turn that example into a bad one; the obligation to follow the model is stated elsewhere.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p101/r2.anchor: والجواب أن جعله مستنكرا ومستثنى يدل على أنه منكر لا الأستثناء عما وجبت فيه فقط

ALUSI-FULL:v16p101/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p101/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p101/r3.claim: Abraham's action was not inherently wrong, but later revelation made such prayer forbidden; whether it had been permitted before the prohibition by reason or by revelation is disputed.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p101/r3.anchor: والحاصل أن فعل إبراهيم عليه السلام يدل على أنه ليس منكرا في نفسه

ALUSI-FULL:v16p101/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p101/r4.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v16p101/r4.claim: Some say pre-prohibition permission followed reason; others, identified as the Sunni view, ground it in revelation because it falls under kindness to parents and compassion for those invited to faith, while the first is attributed to the Muʿtazila.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p101/r4.anchor: إلا أن الزمخشري جعل مدرك الجواز قبل النهي العقل وهي مسئلة خلافية وكم قائل أنه السمع

ALUSI-FULL:v16p101#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p101#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p101#2/r1.claim: An objection says that if Abraham's prayer became forbidden after revelation, the Prophet would not have prayed for Abu Talib; the reply is that he may not yet have received the prohibition.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p101#2/r1.anchor: واعترض القول بأنه استنكر في زمن إبراهيم عليه السلام بعد ما كان غير منكر بأنه لو كان كذلك لم يفعله نبينا

ALUSI-FULL:v16p101#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p101#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p101#2/r2.claim: Seeking faith for a living unbeliever of unknown destiny is permitted by reason and revelation, but not for one known to be sealed against faith; asking forgiveness while one remains an unbeliever is likewise unsound.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p101#2/r2.anchor: أن الأستغفار للكافر الحي المجهول العاقبة بمعنى طلب هدايته للايمان مما لا محذور فيه عقلا ونقلا

ALUSI-FULL:v16p101#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p101#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p101#2/r3.claim: The reason against requesting forgiveness while unbelief continues is that it would trivialize unbelief and make the supreme obligation of faith pointless; the reasoning may extend to other sins, unless unbelief is distinguished.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p101#2/r3.anchor: وصيرورة التكليف بالأيمان الذي لا شئ يعدله من الطاعات عبثا

ALUSI-FULL:v16p101#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p101#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p101#2/r4.claim: Reason alone does not forbid requesting forgiveness for an unbeliever already dead in unbelief; revelation does, because the prior rationale for a living person's continuing unbelief does not apply.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p101#2/r4.anchor: وأما طلب المغفرة للكافر بعد موته على الكفر فلا تأباه قضية العقل وإنما يمنعه السمع

ALUSI-FULL:v16p101#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p101#2/r5.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v16p101#2/r5.claim: One reconciliation says the Prophet continued praying for Abu Talib until 9:113 descended, reading “after it became clear” as after their death in unbelief and placing 4:48 later.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p101#2/r5.anchor: لا ازال أستغفر لك مالم أنه

ALUSI-FULL:v16p101#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p101#2/r6.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v16p101#2/r6.claim: Another reconciliation needs no chronology: out of compassion the Prophet understood that God would not forgive shirk without intercession or involving every limb, believed Abu Talib's shirk was not of that kind, and prayed until forbidden.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p101#2/r6.anchor: وقيل لا حاجة إلى التزام ذلك لجواز أن يكون عليه الصلاة والسلام لو فور شفقة وشدة رافته قد حمل الآية

ALUSI-FULL:v16p102/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p102/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p102/r1.claim: “Kind to me” means abundantly gracious and attentive to honoring Abraham; this explains the preceding promise.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p102/r1.anchor: بليغا في البر والأكرام يقال حفى به اذا اعتنى باكرامه

ALUSI-FULL:v16p102/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p102/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p102/r2.claim: The clause explains the preceding statement, with the adverb moved forward for the verse's cadence and emphasis.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p102/r2.anchor: والجملة تعليل المضمون ماقبلها وتقديم الظرف لرعاية الفواصل مع الأهتمام

ALUSI-FULL:v16p145/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p145/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p145/r7.claim: “Peace be upon you” is read mystically as turning away from worldly others while the righteous remain gentle toward the ignorant.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p145/r7.anchor: قال سلام عليك هذا سلام الاعراض عن الاغيار وتلطف الأبرار مع الجهال

ALUSI-FULL:v16p145/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p145/r8.speaker: أبو بكر بن طاهر
ALUSI-FULL:v16p145/r8.claim: Ibn Tahir says Abraham answered Azar's ignorant speech with peace, following 25:63, then meant that he would leave them for the sake of his religion; this suggests shunning wicked people.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p145/r8.anchor: أنه لما بدا من ازر في خطابه عليه السلام ما لا يبدو إلا من جاهل جعل جوابه السلام

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p235/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p235/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p235/r1.claim: Abraham promises peace meaning he will do his father no harm, since he was not commanded to fight him for disbelief.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p235/r1.anchor: {قال} إبراهيم {سلام عليك} أي سلمت مني لا أصيبك بمكروه، وذلك أنه لم يؤمر بقتاله

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p235/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p235/r2.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p235/r2.claim: Another view understands this as a farewell and separation greeting.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p235/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p235/r3.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p235/r3.claim: A further view takes it as gentle filial kindness, the wise person's reply to a fool, and links it to 25:63.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p235/r3.anchor: وقيل: سلام بر ولطف وهو جواب الحليم للسفيه. قال الله تعالى:

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p235/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p235/r4.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p235/r4.claim: One explanation says that, having exhausted his efforts, Abraham promised to ask God to guide his father to monotheism and forgive him.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p235/r4.anchor: قيل: إنه لما أعياه أمره ووعده أن يراجع الله فيه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p235/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p235/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p235/r5.claim: Seeking forgiveness means asking God to grant his father repentance through which he could receive forgiveness.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p235/r5.anchor: معناه: سأسأل الله تعالى لك توبة تنال بها المغفرة.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p235/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p235/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p235/r6.claim: Being gracious to Abraham means being kind and gentle toward him.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p235/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p235/r7.speaker: الكلبي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p235/r7.claim: Al-Kalbi says God knew Abraham and answered him when he prayed.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p235/r7.anchor: الكلبي: عالما يستجيب لي إذا دعوته.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p235/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p235/r8.speaker: مجاهد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p235/r8.claim: Mujahid says God had made Abraham accustomed to answered prayers.

BAYDAWI-FULL:19:46-47/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:19:46-47/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:19:46-47/r3.claim: Abraham’s peace is farewell and separation, answering injury with kindness; seeking forgiveness for an unbeliever means asking God to guide him to repentance and faith.

BAYDAWI-FULL:19:46-47/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:19:46-47/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:19:46-47/r4.claim: God was abundantly benevolent and gracious to Abraham.

QASHANI:19:42-43/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:19:42-43/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:19:42-43/r3.claim: Abraham's greeting asks God to strip his father's essence of the material veils behind which it is hidden.
QASHANI:19:42-43/r3.anchor: سلام عليك } أي: جرد الله ذاتك عن المواد التي احتجبت بها

QASHANI:19:42-43/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:19:42-43/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:19:42-43/r4.claim: Abraham's promise to seek forgiveness asks God to veil the father's essence in light and erase the veils of his attributes and self-dispositions, if possible.
QASHANI:19:42-43/r4.anchor: سأستغفر لك ربي } سأطلب منه ستر ذاتك بنوره ومحو غشاوات صفاتك بصفاته، ودناءة هيئات نفسك بأفعاله إن أمكن

BIQAI-FULL:v4p538/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p538/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p538/r1.claim: Abraham answers with peace, meaning his father is safe from him unless God commands otherwise.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p538/r1.anchor: أنت سالم مني ما لم أومر فيك بشيء

BIQAI-FULL:v4p538/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p538/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p538/r2.claim: His promise to seek forgiveness means asking God to guide his father to Islam, which erases former sins; Abraham had not yet learned his father was God's enemy and doomed.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p538/r2.anchor: بأن يوفقك للإسلام الجاب لما قبله

BIQAI-FULL:v4p538/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p538/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p538/r3.claim: Abraham trusts God's repeated, exceptional kindness to him, which explains his promise to pray for his father.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p538/r3.anchor: مبالغا في إكرامي مرة بعد مرة

DURR-FULL:v5p512/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p512/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p512/r11.claim: He glosses God's being حفيا to Abraham as being gracious and gentle toward him.
DURR-FULL:v5p512/r11.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله: {إنه كان بي حفيا} قال: لطفيا

DURR-FULL:v5p512/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p512/r12.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v5p512/r12.claim: He says God had repeatedly answered Abraham's prayers.
DURR-FULL:v5p512/r12.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله: {إنه كان بي حفيا} قال: عوده الإجابة

QUSHAYRI:v2p242/r7.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p242/r7.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p242/r7.claim: Abraham's father threatened him after Abraham offered a gracious promise of good; Abraham answered from settled insight while still retaining hope.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p120/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p120/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p120/r5.claim: Abraham’s “peace be upon you” is a farewell of separation, offered before anything else to show he does not resent leaving for God’s sake.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p120/r5.anchor: وبادره به قبل الكلام الذي أعقبه به إشارة إلى أنه لا يسوءه ذلك الهجر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p120/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p120/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p120/r6.claim: Abraham’s forbearance answers his father’s harshness with kindness at their final moment.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p120/r6.anchor: مثوبة بالإحسان في معاملته في آخر لحظة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p120/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p120/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p120/r7.claim: Salām means safety, and ʿalā expresses figurative establishment; the greeting is an expression of honor.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p120/r7.anchor: و ( على ) للاستعلاء المجازي وهو التمكن

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p120/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p120/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p120/r8.claim: Abraham hopes for his father’s guidance and asks forgiveness for past shirk by asking God to guide him to monotheism; no prohibition had yet been revealed, as shown in 9:114 and 26:86.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p120/r8.anchor: بأن يهديه الله إلى التوحيد فيغفر له الشرك الماضي

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p19#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p19#2/r1.speaker: أبو البرهسم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p19#2/r1.claim: Abu al-Barhasm reads salāman in the accusative.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p19#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p19#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p19#2/r2.claim: One group takes Abraham's greeting as a farewell and permits greeting or initiating greeting to an unbeliever.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p19#2/r2.anchor: واختلف أهل العلم في معنى تسليمه عليه، فقال بعضهم هي تحية مفارق وجوزوا تحية الكافر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p19#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p19#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p19#2/r3.claim: The majority understand salām as peaceful parting, not a greeting; al-Tabari glosses it “safety from me for you,” and they oppose initiating a greeting to an unbeliever.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p19#2/r3.anchor: وقال الجمهور: ذلك التسليم بمعنى المسالمة لا بمعنى التحية، قال الطبري معناه أمنة مني لك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p19#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p19#2/r4.speaker: النقاش
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p19#2/r4.claim: Al-Naqqash says a forbearing man addressed a fool gently, like the description of believers' response when the ignorant address them.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p19#2/r4.anchor: وقال النقاش: حليم خاطب سفيها كما قال، وإذا خاطبهم الجاهلون قالوا سلاما

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p19#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p19#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p19#2/r5.claim: Salām is nominative as an indefinite subject because it is specified, and also fits the sense of an accusative “I greet you peacefully”; Sibawayh's example is “a fierce beast provokes a fierce one.”
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p19#2/r5.anchor: ورفع السلام بالابتداء وجاز ذلك مع نكرته لأنها نكرة مخصصة فقربت من المعرفة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p19#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p19#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p19#2/r6.claim: Abraham promises to pray for his father to be guided and forgiven through faith; this is preferable to supposing Abraham thought God forgave unbelievers.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p19#2/r6.anchor: وقوله تعالى سأستغفر معناه سأدعو الله تعالى في أن يهديك فيغفر لك بإيمانك وهذا أظهر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p19#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p19#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p19#2/r7.claim: It is possible Abraham had not yet received the revelation that God does not forgive an unbeliever; he later recognized his father as God's enemy through death or revelation.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p19#2/r7.anchor: وقد يجوز أن يكون إبراهيم عليه السلام أول نبي أوحي إليه أن لا يغفر لكافر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p19#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p19#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p19#2/r8.claim: Makkī's report from al-Suddi that Abraham delayed the prayer until dawn is strained and belongs to the story of Jacob and his sons.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p19#2/r8.anchor: وقال مكي عن السدي: أخره بالاستغفار إلى السحر، وهذا تعسف، وإنما ذكر ذلك في أمر يعقوب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p19#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p19#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p19#2/r9.claim: The future form sa-astaghfiru is apt as a promise of repeated, newly initiated prayer.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p19#2/r9.anchor: وأما هذا فوعد باستغفار كثير مؤتنف فالسين متمكنة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p19#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p19#2/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p19#2/r10.claim: Al-ḥafī means earnest in supplication and gentle; Abraham says this in gratitude for God's favor.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p19#2/r10.anchor: و «الحفي» ، المبتهل المتلطف وهذا شكر من إبراهيم لنعم الله تعالى عليه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p237#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p237#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p237#2/r1.claim: Abraham's greeting means his father is safe from harm; Abraham was not commanded to fight him for disbelief.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p237#2/r1.anchor: أي سلمت من أن أصيبك بمكروه وذلك أنه لم يؤمر بقتاله على كفره

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p237#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p237#2/r2.speaker: ابن الأنباري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p237#2/r2.claim: One view says Abraham would ask God to guide his father to repentance and forgiveness.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p237#2/r2.anchor: المعنى سأسأل الله لك توبة تنال بها مغفرته

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p237#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p237#2/r3.speaker: ابن الأنباري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p237#2/r3.claim: Another view says he promised to seek forgiveness without yet knowing it was forbidden for those persisting in unbelief.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p237#2/r3.anchor: وعده الاستغفار وهو لا يعلم أن ذلك محظور في حق المصرين على الكفر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p237#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p237#2/r4.speaker: ابن أبي طلحة عن ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p237#2/r4.claim: One explanation of ḥafiyyan is gentle, also held by Ibn Zayd and al-Zajjaj.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p237#2/r4.anchor: لطيفا رواه ابن أبي طلحة عن ابن عباس وبه قال ابن زيد والزجاج

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p237#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p237#2/r5.speaker: الضحاك عن ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p237#2/r5.claim: Another explanation of ḥafiyyan is merciful.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p237#2/r5.anchor: والثاني رحيما رواه الضحاك عن ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p237#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p237#2/r6.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p237#2/r6.claim: A third explanation is that God has been benevolent to Abraham and accustomed him to answering his prayers.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p237#2/r6.anchor: بارا عودني منه الإجابة إذا دعوته قاله ابن قتيبة

SULAMI:v1p427#3/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p427#3/r1.speaker: أبو بكر بن طاهر
SULAMI:v1p427#3/r1.claim: After his father spoke ignorantly, invited him to idols, and threatened him, Abraham answered with a peaceful greeting, like the response to ignorant people in 25:63.
SULAMI:v1p427#3/r1.anchor: قال أبو بكر بن طاهر : لما بدا منه كلام الجهال من الدعوة إلى آلهته والوعيد

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p235#2/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p235#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p235#2/r7.claim: Abraham's peaceful farewell echoes believers responding peacefully to ignorant people and withdrawing from vain speech.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p235#2/r7.anchor: كما قال تعالى في صفة المؤمنين: {وإذا خاطبهم الجاهلون قالوا سلاما}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p235#2/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p235#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p235#2/r8.claim: Abraham assures his father he will not harm him, out of respect for their parent-child bond, and says he will ask God to guide and forgive him.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p235#2/r8.anchor: أما أنا فلا ينالك مني مكروه ولا أذى، وذلك لحرمة الأبوة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p235#2/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p235#2/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p235#2/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas and others explain God's attentiveness to Abraham as gentleness in guiding him to sincere worship.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p235#2/r9.anchor: قال ابن عباس وغيره: لطيفا، أي: في أن هداني لعبادته والإخلاص له

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p235#2/r10.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p235#2/r10.speaker: مجاهد، قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p235#2/r10.claim: Mujahid, Qatada, and others explain God's attentiveness as His repeated answering of Abraham's prayers.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p235#2/r10.anchor: وقال مجاهد وقتادة، وغيرهما: {إنه كان بي حفيا} قال (1) : [و] (2) عوده الإجابة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p235#2/r11.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p235#2/r11.speaker: السدي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p235#2/r11.claim: Al-Suddi glosses the description as God caring about Abraham's affairs.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p235#2/r12.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p235#2/r12.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p235#2/r12.claim: Abraham continued seeking forgiveness for his father after migrating, building the sanctuary, and having children, as in his prayer at the Resurrection.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p235#2/r12.anchor: وقد استغفر إبراهيم لأبيه مدة طويلة، وبعد أن هاجر إلى الشام وبنى المسجد الحرام

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p235#2/r13.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p235#2/r13.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p235#2/r13.claim: Early Muslims sought forgiveness for unbelieving relatives by Abraham's example until revelation clarified the exception and prohibited seeking forgiveness after their fate was known.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p235#2/r13.anchor: وقد استغفر المسلمون لقراباتهم وأهليهم من المشركين في ابتداء الإسلام

JISHUMI:v6p4566/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4566/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4566/r10.claim: Ḥafiyy means assiduous, thorough, and exhaustive; related forms describe lavish honoring or intense questioning.
JISHUMI:v6p4566/r10.anchor: والحفي: المستقصي في السؤال، وأصل الباب: الاستقصاء

JISHUMI:v6p4571/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4571/r14.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4571/r14.claim: Seeking forgiveness for an unbeliever is permitted either rationally or on condition he later believes.
JISHUMI:v6p4571/r14.anchor: على جواز الاستغفار للكافر إما عقلا أو بشرط الإيمان

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p23/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p23/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p23/r1.claim: Salāmun ʿalayka may be a farewell and separation, as in 28:55 and 25:63, showing that one may leave someone being advised in such circumstances.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p23/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p23/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p23/r2.claim: Alternatively, Abraham prays for his father's safety to win him over, as shown by his promise to seek forgiveness.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p23/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p23/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p23/r3.claim: Some say the promise of forgiveness presupposed repentance from disbelief, as religious commands addressed to unbelievers presuppose faith and prerequisites such as ablution or the zakat threshold.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p23/r3.anchor: قالوا أراد اشتراط التوبة عن الكفر

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p23/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p23/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p23/r4.claim: Some say Abraham sought forgiveness because his father promised to believe, citing 26:86 and the account of a promise in 9:114.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p23/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p23/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p23/r5.claim: The author objects that only revelation forbids seeking forgiveness for an unbeliever; reason permits the promise and fulfillment before that prohibition, as 60:4 indicates.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p23/r5.anchor: إن الذي منع من الاستغفار للكافر إنما هو السمع

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p23/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p23/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p23/r6.claim: If Abraham had conditioned his promise on faith, it would not have been condemned as an exception to the required example.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p23/r6.anchor: فلو كان شارطا للإيمان لم يكن مستنكرا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p23/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p23/r7.speaker: حماد الراوية
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p23/r7.claim: Hamād's reading, waʿadahā abāhu, supports taking Abraham as the one who promised his father.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p23/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p23/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p23/r8.claim: Ḥafiyyan means exceptionally kind and gracious; the verb is used for being kind to someone.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p23/r8.anchor: البليغ في البر والإلطاف ، حفي به وتحفى به

FARRA:v2p169/r3.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p169/r3.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p169/r3.claim: Ḥafiyyan means knowledgeable and kind toward Abraham, answering whenever he prays.
FARRA:v2p169/r3.anchor: وقوله: كان بي حفيا [47] : كان بي عالما لطيفا يجيب دعائي إذا دعوته.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p374/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p374/r6.speaker: ابن بحر
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p374/r6.claim: Abraham's greeting is a farewell as he leaves his father's place because of unbelief.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p374/r6.anchor: أنه سلام توديع وهجر لمقامه على الكفر , قاله ابن بحر

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p374/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p374/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p374/r7.claim: More apparently, it is a respectful greeting: Abraham answers harshness with filial kindness, recognizing fatherhood and past upbringing.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p374/r7.anchor: وهو أظهر أنه سلام بر وإكرام , فقابل جفوة أبيه بالبر

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p374/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p374/r8.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p374/r8.claim: The promise to seek forgiveness may be conditional on leaving idol worship, or mean praying for guidance that entails forgiveness.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p374/r8.anchor: سأستغفر لك إن تركت عبادة الأوثان . الثاني : معناه سأدعوه لك بالهداية

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p374/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p374/r9.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p374/r9.claim: Hafiyyan means one who draws near, honors, shows mercy (Muqatil), knows (al-Kalbi), or takes care of someone.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p374/r9.anchor: مقربا . الثاني : مكرما . الثالث : رحيما , قاله مقاتل

MUQATIL:19:45-48/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:19:45-48/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:19:45-48/r5.claim: Ibrahim answers with peace and promises to ask his Lord to forgive his father, since God has been gracious and gentle toward him.
MUQATIL:19:45-48/r5.anchor: سلام عليك سأستغفر لك ربي إنه كان بي حفيا } [آية: 47]، يعني لطيفا رحيما.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p39#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p39#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p39#2/r1.claim: سلام عليك may be a farewell and separation or a kindly, conciliatory parting; this explains his promise to seek forgiveness.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p39#2/r1.anchor: سلام توديع ومتاركة أو تقريب وملاطفة ولذا وعد بالاستغفار

NASAFI-FULL:v3p39#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p39#2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p39#2/r2.claim: Seeking forgiveness means asking God to make Azar among those forgiven by guiding him to Islam.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p39#2/r2.anchor: سأسأل الله أن يجعلك من أهل المغفرة بأن يهديك للاسلام

NASAFI-FULL:v3p39#2/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p39#2/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p39#2/r3.claim: Ḥafiyyan means graciously gentle through blessings, merciful, or honoring; ḥifāwah denotes compassion, mercy, or honor.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p39#2/r3.anchor: ملطفا بعموم النعم أو رحيما أو مكرما والحفاوة الرأفة والرحمة والكرامة

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p274#6/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p274#6/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p274#6/r1.claim: Ḥafiyyan means kindly and beneficent; God has accustomed Abraham to an answer whenever he prays.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p274#6/r1.anchor: {إنه كان بي حفيا} أي بارا عودني منه الإجابة إذا دعوته.

MAJAZ:v2p8/r1.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p8/r1.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p8/r1.claim: حفيا means showing special care or kindness, from تحفيت بفلان.
MAJAZ:v2p8/r1.anchor: «كان بي حفيا» (47) أي متحفيا، يقال: تحفيت بفلان

QURTUBI-FULL:19:47/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:47/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:19:47/r2.claim: Abraham did not answer his father harshly because he had not been commanded to fight him for disbelief.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:47/r2.anchor: لم يعارضه إبراهيم عليه السلام بسوء الرد لأنه لم يؤمر بقتاله على كفره

QURTUBI-FULL:19:47/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:47/r3.speaker: الجمهور
QURTUBI-FULL:19:47/r3.claim: Most interpreters take Abraham’s greeting as peaceful disengagement rather than a salutation; al-Tabari glosses it as safety from him, which supports not initiating greetings with unbelievers.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:47/r3.anchor: والجمهور على أن المراد بسلامه المسالمة التي هي المتاركة لا التحية

QURTUBI-FULL:19:47/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:47/r4.speaker: النقاش
QURTUBI-FULL:19:47/r4.claim: Al-Naqqash says Abraham, being forbearing, answered a fool gently, as in the verse about servants of the Merciful.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:47/r4.anchor:
حليم خاطب سفيها كما قال:
وإذا خاطبهم الجاهلون قالوا سلاما

QURTUBI-FULL:19:47/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:47/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:19:47/r5.claim: Some take Abraham’s words as a farewell greeting, allowing a greeting to an unbeliever and permitting one to initiate it.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:47/r5.anchor: هو تحية مفارق وجوز تحية الكافر وأن يبدأ بها

QURTUBI-FULL:19:47/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:47/r6.speaker: سفيان بن عيينة
QURTUBI-FULL:19:47/r6.claim: Sufyan ibn Uyayna permits greeting a non-hostile unbeliever, citing God’s permission to treat them kindly and Abraham’s example.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:47/r6.anchor: قيل لابن عيينة: هل يجوز السلام على الكافر؟ قال: نعم

QURTUBI-FULL:19:47/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:47/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:19:47/r7.claim: Qurtubi says the strongest reading of the verse is Sufyan ibn Uyayna’s permission to greet unbelievers.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:47/r7.anchor: قلت: الأظهر من الآية ما قاله سفيان بن عيينة

QURTUBI-FULL:19:47/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:47/r8.speaker: أبو هريرة
QURTUBI-FULL:19:47/r8.claim: A sound report from Abu Hurayra says the Prophet forbade initiating greetings to Jews and Christians and instructed Muslims to make them take the narrower side of the road.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:47/r8.anchor:
روى أبو هريرة أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال:
" لا تبدؤوا اليهود والنصارى بالسلام

QURTUBI-FULL:19:47/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:47/r9.speaker: أسامة بن زيد
QURTUBI-FULL:19:47/r9.claim: A report in both Sahihs from Usama ibn Zayd describes the Prophet greeting a mixed gathering of Muslims, polytheists, and Jews while visiting Sa‘d ibn Ubada before Badr.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:47/r9.anchor:
وفي الصحيحين عن أسامة بن زيد:
" أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ركب حمارا

QURTUBI-FULL:19:47-50/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:47-50/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:19:47-50/r1.claim: The first report disallows initiating greetings to unbelievers because it honors them; a second permits it, and al-Tabari reconciles the reports as general and specific.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:47-50/r1.anchor: فالأول يفيد ترك السلام عليهم ابتداء، لأن ذلك إكرام، والكافر ليس أهله.

QURTUBI-FULL:19:47-50/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:47-50/r2.speaker: النخعي
QURTUBI-FULL:19:47-50/r2.claim: Al-Nakhai permits greeting a Jew or Christian first when there is a need involving them.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:47-50/r2.anchor: وقال النخعي: إذا كانت لك حاجة عند يهودي أو نصراني فابدأه بالسلام فبان بهذا أن حديث أبي هريرة " لا تبدؤوهم بالسلام "

QURTUBI-FULL:19:47-50/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:47-50/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:19:47-50/r3.claim: The prohibition applies when there is no reason to greet first, such as a need, companionship, neighborly right, or travel.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:47-50/r3.anchor: إذا كان لغير سبب يدعوكم إلى أن تبدؤوهم بالسلام، من قضاء ذمام أو حاجة تعرض لكم قبلهم، أو حق صحبة أو جوار أو سفر.

QURTUBI-FULL:19:47-50/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:47-50/r4.speaker: ابن مسعود
QURTUBI-FULL:19:47-50/r4.claim: Ibn Masud greeted a Persian notable who traveled with him; he explained to Alqama that companionship carries a right to greet.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:47-50/r4.anchor: وفعله ابن مسعود بدهقان صحبه في طريقه قال علقمة: فقلت له يا أبا عبد الرحمن أليس يكره أن يبدؤوا بالسلام؟!

QURTUBI-FULL:19:47-50/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:47-50/r5.speaker: أبو أسامة
QURTUBI-FULL:19:47-50/r5.claim: Abu Usama greeted every passerby, Muslim or non-Muslim, young or old, because Muslims are commanded to spread greetings.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:47-50/r5.anchor: وكان أبو أسامة إذا انصرف إلى بيته لا يمر بمسلم ولا نصراني ولا صغير ولا كبير إلا سلم عليه فقيل له في ذلك فقال: أمرنا أن نفشي السلام.

QURTUBI-FULL:19:47-50/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:47-50/r6.speaker: الأوزاعي
QURTUBI-FULL:19:47-50/r6.claim: Al-Awzai says both greeting and withholding a greeting from a non-Muslim follow precedents of earlier righteous people.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:47-50/r6.anchor: وسئل الأوزاعي عن مسلم مر بكافر فسلم عليه، فقال: إن سلمت فقد سلم الصالحون قبلك، وإن تركت فقد ترك الصالحون قبلك.

QURTUBI-FULL:19:47-50/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:47-50/r7.speaker: الحسن البصري
QURTUBI-FULL:19:47-50/r7.claim: Hasan al-Basri says to greet a gathering that contains Muslims and unbelievers.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:47-50/r7.anchor: وروي عن الحسن البصري أنه قال: إذا مررت بمجلس فيه مسلمون وكفار فسلم عليهم.

QURTUBI-FULL:19:47-50/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:47-50/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:19:47-50/r8.claim: The stricter camp argues salam as greeting is distinctive to this community, citing Anas's report that it is the greeting of Paradise.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:47-50/r8.anchor: لحديث أنس بن مالك قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: " إن الله تعالى أعطى أمتي ثلاثا لم تعط أحدا قبلهم السلام وهي تحية أهل الجنة "

QURTUBI-FULL:19:47-50/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:47-50/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:19:47-50/r9.claim: Salam is nominative as the subject; its indefinite form is allowed because it is restricted and paired with a definite expression.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:47-50/r9.anchor: وارتفع السلام بالابتداء، وجاز ذلك مع نكرته لأنه نكرة مخصصة فقرنت المعرفة.

QURTUBI-FULL:19:47-50/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:47-50/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:19:47-50/r10.claim: Hafiy means abundant kindness and gracious treatment; al-Kisai gives dialectal forms حفاوة and حفوة for the same idea.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:47-50/r10.anchor: قوله تعالى: { إنه كان بي حفيا }: الحفي المبالغ في البر والإلطاف يقال: حفي به وتحفى إذا بره.

QURTUBI-FULL:19:47-50/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:47-50/r11.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:19:47-50/r11.claim: Al-Farra glosses the phrase as God knowing and gently answering when Abraham calls Him.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:47-50/r11.anchor: وقال الفراء: { إنه كان بي حفيا } أي عالما لطيفا يجيبني إذا دعوته.

RAZI-FULL:v21p195#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p195#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p195#2/r2.claim: Abraham’s “peace be on you” is a farewell and truce, like the replies in al-Qasas and al-Furqan.
RAZI-FULL:v21p195#2/r2.anchor: وقوله : { سلام عليك } توادع ومتاركة كقوله تعالى : { لنا أعمالنا ولكم أعمالكم سلام عليكم

RAZI-FULL:v21p195#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p195#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p195#2/r3.claim: This supports disengaging from an advised person who persists obstinately and answering abuse with kindness.
RAZI-FULL:v21p195#2/r3.anchor: وهذا دليل على جواز متاركة المنصوح إذا ظهر منه اللجاج ، وعلى أنه تحسن مقابلة الإساءة بالإحسان

RAZI-FULL:v21p195#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p195#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p195#2/r4.claim: Alternatively, Abraham prayed for his father’s safety to win him over, as shown by the accompanying promise to seek forgiveness.
RAZI-FULL:v21p195#2/r4.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون قد دعا له بالسلامة استمالة له ، ألا ترى أنه وعده بالاستغفار

RAZI-FULL:v21p195#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p195#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p195#2/r5.claim: Although he leaves, Abraham’s concern for his father remains, as his promise to seek forgiveness shows.
RAZI-FULL:v21p195#2/r5.anchor: ضم إلى ذلك ما دل به على أنه وإن بعد عنه فاشفاقه باق عليه كما كان

RAZI-FULL:v21p195#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p195#2/r6.speaker: من طعن في عصمة الأنبياء
RAZI-FULL:v21p195#2/r6.claim: Critics argue that Abraham sinned by seeking forgiveness for his unbelieving father, since the Qur’an and consensus establish the father’s unbelief and forbid seeking forgiveness for unbelievers.
RAZI-FULL:v21p195#2/r6.anchor: واحتج بهذه الآية من طعن في عصمة الأنبياء ، وتقريره أن إبراهيم عليه السلام فعل ما لا يجوز

RAZI-FULL:v21p195#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p195#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p195#2/r7.claim: First reply: certainty that God will punish a disbeliever depends on revelation; Abraham’s law may not have established that certainty.
RAZI-FULL:v21p195#2/r7.anchor: أن القطع على أن الله تعالى يعذب الكافر لا يعرف إلا بالسمع ، فلعل إبراهيم عليه السلام لم يجد

RAZI-FULL:v21p195#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p195#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p195#2/r8.claim: Second reply: seeking forgiveness may mean asking God to spare the father immediate worldly punishment while he lived, as in al-Jathiya.
RAZI-FULL:v21p195#2/r8.anchor: أن الاستغفار قد يكون بمعنى الاستماحة ، كما في قوله : { قل للذين ءامنوا يغفروا للذين لا يرجون أيام الله

RAZI-FULL:v21p195#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p195#2/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p195#2/r9.claim: Third reply: Abraham hoped his father would believe; his law may have permitted praying for a disbeliever expected to believe, and the ban applies after knowing someone is destined for Hell.
RAZI-FULL:v21p195#2/r9.anchor: إنما استغفر لأبيه لأنه كان يرجو منه الإيمان فلما أيس من ذلك ترك الاستغفار

RAZI-FULL:v21p195#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p195#2/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p195#2/r10.claim: Al-Tawba explains that Abraham’s promise was conditional on his father believing; when the father did not believe, Abraham ceased and disavowed him.
RAZI-FULL:v21p195#2/r10.anchor: وما كان استغفار إبراهيم لابيه إلا عن موعدة وعدها إياه فلما تبين له أنه عدو لله تبرأ منه

RAZI-FULL:v21p195#2/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p195#2/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p195#2/r11.claim: The prohibition on taking Abraham as an example in this act does not prove it was sinful, since prophets can have lawful acts that are special to them.
RAZI-FULL:v21p195#2/r11.anchor: لكن المنع من التأسي به في ذلك لا يدل على أن ذلك كان معصية . فإن كثيرا من الأشياء

RAZI-FULL:v21p195#2/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p195#2/r12.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p195#2/r12.claim: A fourth reply is that the prayer may have been a permissible but less-preferred act, as good deeds of the righteous can be shortcomings for those nearest to God.
RAZI-FULL:v21p195#2/r12.anchor: لعل هذا الاستغفار كان من باب ترك الأولى وحسنات الأبرار سيئآت المقربين

RAZI-FULL:v21p195#2/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p195#2/r13.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p195#2/r13.claim: Hafiyyan means gentle, gracious, and exceptionally kind, from the idiom for treating a petitioner gently, as in Muhammad.
RAZI-FULL:v21p195#2/r13.anchor: أي لطيفا رفيقا يقال أحفى فلان في المسألة بفلان إذا لطف به وبالغ في الرفق

RAZI-FULL:v21p195#2/r14.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p195#2/r14.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p195#2/r14.claim: God’s kindness and generosity had accustomed Abraham to answered prayers, so he speaks as confident that repentance would bring his father forgiveness.
RAZI-FULL:v21p195#2/r14.anchor: لطفه بي وإنعامه على عودني الإجابة فإذا أنا استغفرت لك حصل المراد

STUDYQURAN:19:47/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:19:47/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:19:47/r1.claim: Peace is a greeting of believers in this world and Paradise and a prescribed response to ignorant or idle speech.
STUDYQURAN:19:47/r1.anchor: the greeting of the believers, both in this world and in Paradise

STUDYQURAN:19:47/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:19:47/r2.speaker: Quran commentators
STUDYQURAN:19:47/r2.claim: Here Abraham's peace is not a greeting but a promise to end the confrontation without fighting and to reassure his father.
STUDYQURAN:19:47/r2.anchor: an indication that he will discontinue his confrontation with his father

STUDYQURAN:19:47/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:19:47/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:19:47/r3.claim: Abraham asks forgiveness for his father, but later disavows him once his enmity toward God becomes clear.
STUDYQURAN:19:47/r3.anchor: when it became clear to him that his father was an enemy of God, he repudiated him

NAHHAS:v3p18/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p18/r5.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p18/r5.claim: The indefinite سلام can begin a sentence because it carries greeting and separation, as in the greeting of the ignorant.
NAHHAS:v3p18/r5.anchor: صلح الابتداء بالنكرة لأن فيها معنى المنصوب وفيها في هذا الموضع

NAHHAS:v3p18/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p18/r6.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p18/r6.claim: The statement means if you submit and repent; Ibn ʿAbbās glosses حفي as gentle, al-Kisāʾī as showing kindness, al-Farrāʾ as knowing and answering, and Abū Isḥāq as treating graciously.
NAHHAS:v3p18/r6.anchor: أي إن أسلمت وتبت ( إنه كان بي حفيا ) قال علي بن أبي طلحة عن ابن عباس

TAB-FULL:v15p556/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p556/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p556/r3.claim: God has been kind and responsive to Abraham's prayer; ḥafiyy means gentle or kind, from a verb for treating someone gently.
TAB-FULL:v15p556/r3.anchor: يقول: إن ربي عهدته بي لطيفا يجيب دعائي إذا دعوته يقال منه: تحفى بي فلان.

TAB-FULL:v15p556/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p556/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v15p556/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses God being ḥafiyy to Abraham as being kind.
TAB-FULL:v15p556/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {إنه كان بي حفيا} [مريم: 47] يقول: لطيفا

TAB-FULL:v15p556/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p556/r5.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v15p556/r5.claim: Ibn Zayd likewise glosses ḥafiyy as kind or gentle.
TAB-FULL:v15p556/r5.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: {إنه كان بي حفيا} [مريم: 47] قال: إنه كان بي لطيفا، فإن الحفي: اللطيف

TABATABAI:19:44-47/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:44-47/r7.speaker: الراغب
TABATABAI:19:44-47/r7.claim: Al-Rāghib explains ḥafiyy as kindly and attentive to fine needs, meeting them successively and well.
TABATABAI:19:44-47/r7.anchor: الحفي على ما ذكره الراغب البر اللطيف وهو الذي يتتبع دقائق الحوائج

TABATABAI:19:44-47/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:44-47/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:44-47/r8.claim: Abraham answers the threat and expulsion with a peace that offers safety, promises to ask God’s forgiveness, and says he will leave the people and their gods.
TABATABAI:19:44-47/r8.anchor: قابل إبراهيم عليه السلام أباه فيما أساء إليه وهدده وفيه سلب الأمن عنه من قبله بالسلام

TABATABAI:19:46-47/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:46-47/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:46-47/r1.claim: Peace is the conduct of the generous; Abraham answers ignorance graciously, as in 25:72 and 25:63.
TABATABAI:19:46-47/r1.anchor: أما السلام فهو من دأب الكرام قابل به جهالة أبيه

TABATABAI:19:46-47/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:46-47/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:46-47/r2.claim: He rejects reading Abraham’s greeting as a farewell: Abraham left his father and people only after some time.
TABATABAI:19:46-47/r2.anchor: ففيه أنه اعتزله وقومه بعد مدة غير قصيرة

TABATABAI:19:46-47/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:46-47/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:46-47/r3.claim: Abraham was not yet sure that his father was a hardened enemy of God; he may have been an ignorant, vulnerable person who would follow truth if it became clear.
TABATABAI:19:46-47/r3.anchor: أنه عليه السلام لم يكن وقتئذ قاطعا بكونه من أولياء الشيطان أي مطبوعا على قلبه بالشرك

TABATABAI:19:46-47/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:46-47/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:46-47/r4.claim: Abraham offers intercession as hope, not a guarantee; the author supports this by the later command to disavow his father once his enmity became clear.
TABATABAI:19:46-47/r4.anchor: فاستعطفه عليه السلام بوعد الاستغفار ولم يحتم له المغفرة بل أظهر الرجاء

TABATABAI:19:47-50/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:47-50/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:47-50/r1.claim: God permits kindness and fairness toward people who have not fought or expelled believers, supporting Abraham’s earlier hope for his father.
TABATABAI:19:47-50/r1.anchor: لا ينهاكم الله عن الذين لم يقاتلوكم في الدين ولم يخرجوكم من دياركم أن تبروهم

TABATABAI:19:47-50/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:47-50/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:47-50/r2.claim: He rejects the view that Abraham’s promise followed reason’s permission and was later barred by religious law; it fails to fit the narrative context.
TABATABAI:19:47-50/r2.anchor: أنه وعده الاستغفار واستغفر له بمقتضى العقل فإن العقل لا يأبى عن تجويزه

TABATABAI:19:47-50/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:47-50/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:47-50/r3.claim: He also rejects construing the promise as conditional on the father’s repentance or as a request only to avert worldly punishment, since neither restriction is stated.
TABATABAI:19:47-50/r3.anchor: ومنها أن معنى استغفاره كان مشروطا بتوبته وإيمانه. وهو كما ترى

TABATABAI:19:47-50/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:47-50/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:47-50/r4.claim: The fairest alternative is that asking forgiveness implies asking God to grant repentance and faith, though the author finds it somewhat remote because forgiveness better suits the appeal’s tenderness.
TABATABAI:19:47-50/r4.anchor: وهذا وإن كان أعدل الوجوه لكنه لا يخلو عن بعد لأن في الكلام استعطافا

TABRISI:19:41-44/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:41-44/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:19:41-44/r6.claim: Ḥafiyy is one who investigates insistently; khafiyy is gentle in extending favor, from a root of scrutiny.
TABRISI:19:41-44/r6.anchor: والحفي المستقصي في السؤال والخفي اللطيف بعموم النعمة وأصل الباب الاستقصاء

TABRISI:19:41-44/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:41-44/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:19:41-44/r7.claim: A line by ʿĀmir ibn al-Ḥārith illustrates use of lisān for someone's praise or blame.
TABRISI:19:41-44/r7.anchor: وتقول العرب جاءني لسان فلان أي مدحه وذمه قال عامر بن الحرث

TABRISI:19:45-48/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:45-48/r15.speaker: الجبائي وأبو مسلم
TABRISI:19:45-48/r15.claim: Ibrahim's salām is a gentle farewell and separation from his father.
TABRISI:19:45-48/r15.anchor: سلام توديع وهجر على ألطف الوجوه وهو سلام متاركة ومباعدة منه عن الجبائي وأبي مسلم

TABRISI:19:45-48/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:45-48/r16.speaker: author
TABRISI:19:45-48/r16.claim: Alternatively, it is an honorable greeting: Ibrahim repays his father's harshness kindly and leaves without disobedience.
TABRISI:19:45-48/r16.anchor: وقيل: هذا سلام إكرام وبر فقابل جفوة أبيه بالبر تأدية لحق الأبوة

TABRISI:19:45-48/r17.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:45-48/r17.speaker: الجبائي
TABRISI:19:45-48/r17.claim: One view says Ibrahim promised to seek forgiveness before its prohibition for polytheists was established.
TABRISI:19:45-48/r17.anchor: أنه إنما وعده بالاستغفار على مقتضى العقل ولم يكن بعد قد استقر قبح الاستغفار للمشركين

TABRISI:19:45-48/r18.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:45-48/r18.speaker: الجبائي
TABRISI:19:45-48/r18.claim: Another view makes the promise conditional on his father's abandoning idol worship and devoting worship to God.
TABRISI:19:45-48/r18.anchor: أنه قال سأستغفر لك ربي على ما يصح ويجوز من تركك عبادة الأوثان

TABRISI:19:45-48/r19.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:45-48/r19.speaker: الأصم
TABRISI:19:45-48/r19.claim: A third view interprets the prayer as asking God not to punish the father in this world.
TABRISI:19:45-48/r19.anchor: وثالثها: أن معناه سأدعو الله أن لا يعذبك في الدنيا عن الأصم

TABRISI:19:45-48/r20.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:45-48/r20.speaker: ابن عباس ومقاتل
TABRISI:19:45-48/r20.claim: Ḥafiyyan means kind, gentle, and merciful to Ibrahim.
TABRISI:19:45-48/r20.anchor: أي بارا لطيفا رحيما عن ابن عباس ومقاتل

TABRISI:19:45-48/r21.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:45-48/r21.speaker: author
TABRISI:19:45-48/r21.claim: Alternatively, God had made a practice of showing Ibrahim kindness and honoring him.
TABRISI:19:45-48/r21.anchor: وقيل: إن الله عودني إحسانه وكان لي مكرما

TABRISI:19:45-48/r22.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:45-48/r22.speaker: author
TABRISI:19:45-48/r22.claim: Another explanation is that God knows Ibrahim and what he hopes to achieve by striving to guide his father.
TABRISI:19:45-48/r22.anchor: وقيل: كان عالما بي وبما أبتغيه من مجالدتك لعله يهديك

THALABI:v6p217/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p217/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p217/r1.claim: Abraham’s greeting means that his father is safe from harm at Abraham’s hands.
THALABI:v6p217/r1.anchor: قال إبراهيم سلام عليك أي سلمت مني لا أصيبك بمكروه

THALABI:v6p217/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p217/r2.speaker: ابن عباس ومقاتل
THALABI:v6p217/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas and Muqatil explain ḥafiyyan as gentle and merciful.
THALABI:v6p217/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس ومقاتل: لطيفا رحيما

THALABI:v6p217/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p217/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p217/r3.claim: Another gloss for ḥafiyyan is kind and devoted.

THALABI:v6p217/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p217/r4.speaker: مجاهد
THALABI:v6p217/r4.claim: Mujahid says the phrase means God has made a habit of answering Abraham.

THALABI:v6p217/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p217/r5.speaker: الكلبي
THALABI:v6p217/r5.claim: Al-Kalbi says Abraham knew God would answer when called upon.
THALABI:v6p217/r5.anchor: وقال الكلبي: عالما يستجيب لي إذا دعوته

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p258/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p258/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p258/r1.claim: Abraham means that his father is safe from harm by him; he does not have an order to fight his father over unbelief.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p258/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p258/r2.speaker: سفيان بن عيينة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p258/r2.claim: He permits greeting non-Muslims in wartime but not in peace, citing the command to treat noncombatants kindly and Abraham as an example; Abraham's model explicitly excludes asking forgiveness, not greeting.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p258/r2.anchor: سفيان بن عيينة: (أيجوز السلام على أهل الذمة؟ فقال: نعم، إنما حضر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p258/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p258/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p258/r3.claim: Abraham promises to pray for repentance and monotheism as well as forgiveness, since forgiveness cannot be granted while his father persists in associationism; when his father's enmity to God became clear, Abraham disavowed him.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p258/r3.anchor: سأسأل الله لك توبة تنال بها مغفرته

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p258/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p258/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p258/r4.claim: Another view says Abraham promised before knowing prayer for a person persisting in unbelief was forbidden, then stopped after God informed him.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p258/r4.anchor: وعد أباه الاستغفار وهو لا يعلم أن ذلك محظور على المصر على الكفر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p259/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p259/r1.speaker: ابن عباس ومقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p259/r1.claim: They explain حفيا as kind and gentle, as do most exegetes; al-Zajjaj cites the verb for treating someone kindly.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p259/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p259/r2.speaker: الكلبي وابن عباس، رواية عطاء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p259/r2.claim: Another interpretation makes حفيا mean knowing; Jabir says it means a helper, and al-Farra reports both interpretations.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p259/r2.anchor: (¬5). والكلام في هذا قد مر مستقصى في قوله: {يسألونك كأنك حفي

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p259/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p259/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p259/r3.claim: The word was discussed more fully at 7:187.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p259/r3.anchor: والكلام في هذا قد مر مستقصى في قوله: {يسألونك كأنك حفي عنها}

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:47-50/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:47-50/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:47-50/r1.claim: Abraham's peace means he will not harm his father; the author compares it with the reply to ignorant speakers.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:47-50/r1.anchor: سلام عليك } أي: سلمت مني لا أصيبك بمكروه، وهذا جواب الجاهل، كقوله:

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:47-50/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:47-50/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:47-50/r2.claim: The quoted response says that when addressed by the ignorant, God's servants say peace.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:47-50/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:47-50/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:47-50/r3.claim: Abraham promised to seek forgiveness before he was prohibited from doing so for his father, hoping it would be answered; hafiyyan means kind and gracious.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:47-50/r3.anchor: سأستغفر لك ربي } كان هذا قبل أن نهي عن استغفاره، وعده ذلك رجاء أن يجاب فيه { إنه كان بي حفيا } بارا لطيفا.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p227/r8.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p227/r8.speaker: السدي
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p227/r8.claim: Al-Suddī interprets Abraham's greeting to his father as returning a good response.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p227/r8.anchor: يعني رد خيرا في تفسير السدي

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p227/r9.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p227/r9.speaker: الحسن
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p227/r9.claim: Al-Hasan calls Abraham's 'peace be upon you' a word of forbearance.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p227/r10.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p227/r10.speaker: الحسن
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p227/r10.claim: Al-Hasan explains God's being attentive to Abraham as answering his prayer rather than rejecting it.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p227/r10.anchor: بدعائي فلا يرده علي في تفسير الحسن

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p227/r11.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p227/r11.speaker: الكلبي
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p227/r11.claim: Al-Kalbī glosses God's care for Abraham as mercy.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p227/r11.anchor: وفي تفسير الكلبي: إنه كان بي رحيما

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p227/r12.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p227/r12.speaker: بعضهم
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p227/r12.claim: Some explain God's care for Abraham as gentleness.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p227/r13.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p227/r13.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p227/r13.claim: Abraham's promised request for forgiveness is linked to Qur'an 9:114, which says he had promised his father this.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p227/r13.anchor: فهو قوله: {وما كان استغفار إبراهيم لأبيه إلا عن موعدة وعدها إياه} [التوبة: 114]

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:42/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:42/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:42/r3.claim: Abraham promised to seek forgiveness before learning his father would die an unbeliever and enemy of God; then he stopped praying for him.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:42/r3.anchor: Bu durumu öğrenince babasının affı için dua etmekten vazgeçti

SAMIN-DURR:19:47/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:19:47/r1.speaker: أبو البرهسم
SAMIN-DURR:19:47/r1.claim: Abu al-Barhasam reads سلاما in the accusative; the author says its parsing follows the previously discussed analysis.
SAMIN-DURR:19:47/r1.anchor: وقرأ أبو البرهسم " سلاما " بالنصب، وتوجيهها واضح مما تقدم.

ZAJJAJ:v3p332#2/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p332#2/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p332#2/r1.claim: حفيّا means kind and gentle; تحفى به describes treating someone with care and kindness.
ZAJJAJ:v3p332#2/r1.anchor: معناه لطيفا، يقال: قد تحفى فلان بفلان

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Abraham's promise to seek forgiveness despite his father's callousness exemplifies his softness, sympathy, and love.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: the promise by Abraham (sws) to pray for his forgiveness shows how soft, sympathetic and loving he was.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Salām is an affectionate farewell formula as well as a blessed greeting when people meet.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: greet people when meeting them, at the time of departing too it is a very affectionate way of expressing farewell.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The description of God as ḥafī means affectionate, caring, and kind; Abraham's offer to pray for his hostile father shows his tenderness, and he continued until God stopped him.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: The word ﺣَrefers to someone who is very affectionate, caring and kind.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Abraham's promise to seek forgiveness demonstrates his love despite his father's callousness; Qur'anic instances show he kept praying until God stopped him.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: he kept making this prayer until the Almighty stopped him.

QIRAAT-ER:19:47:6#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:19:47:6#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:19:47:6#1/r1.claim: Full voweling of the final yāʾ is a canonical phonological variant with the same meaning.
QIRAAT-ER:19:47:6#1/r1.anchor: Full voweling of the final yāʾ — same semantic content, differs only in phonological realization

SIBAWAYH:وذلكلأنهالحقتماقدعملفيهغيرهاكما.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكلأنهالحقتماقدعملفيهغيرهاكما.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكلأنهالحقتماقدعملفيهغيرهاكما.claim: When لا precedes an invocation noun already governed as a noun, it leaves the phrase in its prior nominal form; it need not be dualized.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكلأنهالحقتماقدعملفيهغيرهاكما.anchor: لا مرحبا ولا أهلا ولا كرامة ولا مسرة

SIBAWAYH:وذلكلأنهالحقتماقدعملفيهغيرهاكما.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكلأنهالحقتماقدعملفيهغيرهاكما.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكلأنهالحقتماقدعملفيهغيرهاكما.claim: لا سلام عليك retains the phrase's form; Jarir's لا سلام على عمرو parallels the verbal prayer لا سلم الله عليه.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكلأنهالحقتماقدعملفيهغيرهاكما.anchor: لا سلام عليك لم تغير الكلام

SIBAWAYH:وذلكلأنهالحقتماقدعملفيهغيرهاكما.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكلأنهالحقتماقدعملفيهغيرهاكما.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكلأنهالحقتماقدعملفيهغيرهاكما.claim: لا بك السوء is a prayer meaning لا ساءك الله.

SIBAWAYH:وذلكلأنهالحقتماقدعملفيهغيرهاكما.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكلأنهالحقتماقدعملفيهغيرهاكما.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكلأنهالحقتماقدعملفيهغيرهاكما.claim: لا also joins expressions of wishing and gracious welcome, as it does their verbal equivalents such as لا أكرمك and لا أسرك.

SIBAWAYH:وذلكلأنهالحقتماقدعملفيهغيرهاكما.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكلأنهالحقتماقدعملفيهغيرهاكما.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكلأنهالحقتماقدعملفيهغيرهاكما.claim: The noun construction is supported by the corresponding verbal construction: the imperative لا اضرب is not available, so the nominal form follows the preexisting noun pattern.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكلأنهالحقتماقدعملفيهغيرهاكما.anchor: لأنه لا يجوز لا اضرب في الأمر

SIBAWAYH:وذلكلأنهالحقتماقدعملفيهغيرهاكما.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكلأنهالحقتماقدعملفيهغيرهاكما.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكلأنهالحقتماقدعملفيهغيرهاكما.claim: لا سواء is possible because لا substitutes for what سواء was predicated of; the same replacement explains لاها الله ذا.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكلأنهالحقتماقدعملفيهغيرهاكما.anchor: ألا ترى أنك لا تقول هذان سواء

SIBAWAYH:وذلكلأنهالحقتماقدعملفيهغيرهاكما.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكلأنهالحقتماقدعملفيهغيرهاكما.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكلأنهالحقتماقدعملفيهغيرهاكما.claim: لا نولك أن تفعل substitutes for لا ينبغي أن تفعل, so لا enters the construction as it enters ينبغي.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكلأنهالحقتماقدعملفيهغيرهاكما.anchor: أن تفعل لأنهم جعلوه معاقبا لقوله

SIBAWAYH:وذلكلأنهالحقتماقدعملفيهغيرهاكما.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكلأنهالحقتماقدعملفيهغيرهاكما.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكلأنهالحقتماقدعملفيهغيرهاكما.claim: In بلا ذنب and similar phrases, لا with ب functions as one unit meaning without; بغير ذنب is the paraphrase when غير is not treated as an actual object.

SIBAWAYH:وذلكلأنهالحقتماقدعملفيهغيرهاكما.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكلأنهالحقتماقدعملفيهغيرهاكما.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكلأنهالحقتماقدعملفيهغيرهاكما.claim: The construction لا شيء can diminish a matter, as in ما كان إلا كلا شيء and أنك ولا شيئا سواء.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكلأنهالحقتماقدعملفيهغيرهاكما.anchor: إلا كلا شئ وأنك ولا شيئا سواء

SIBAWAYH:وذلكلأنهالحقتماقدعملفيهغيرهاكما.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكلأنهالحقتماقدعملفيهغيرهاكما.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكلأنهالحقتماقدعملفيهغيرهاكما.claim: With حين لا حين, لا is treated as null; when لا براح or لا مستصرخ is accusative, that is the commoner construction, while nominative is also Arabic.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكلأنهالحقتماقدعملفيهغيرهاكما.anchor: والنصب أجود وأكثر من الرفع لأنك إذا قلت لا غلام فهي أكثر

SIBAWAYH:وذلكلأنهالحقتماقدعملفيهغيرهاكما.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكلأنهالحقتماقدعملفيهغيرهاكما.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكلأنهالحقتماقدعملفيهغيرهاكما.claim: A predicate لا فارس is awkward unless paired with a contrasting description, because it answers an implied choice between فارس and شجاع.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكلأنهالحقتماقدعملفيهغيرهاكما.anchor: حتى تقول لا فارس ولا شجاع

SIBAWAYH:وذلكلأنهالحقتماقدعملفيهغيرهاكما.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكلأنهالحقتماقدعملفيهغيرهاكما.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكلأنهالحقتماقدعملفيهغيرهاكما.claim: A poet of Banū Sulūl uses the otherwise weak unpaired description لا نفع, showing the construction can occur in poetry.

SIBAWAYH:وذلكلأنهالحقتماقدعملفيهغيرهاكما.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكلأنهالحقتماقدعملفيهغيرهاكما.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكلأنهالحقتماقدعملفيهغيرهاكما.claim: In questions, لا governs what follows just as in statements; Ḥassān's line supplies an example.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكلأنهالحقتماقدعملفيهغيرهاكما.anchor: واعلم أن لا في الاستفهام تعمل فيما بعدها

SIBAWAYH:وذلكلأنهالحقتماقدعملفيهغيرهاكما.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكلأنهالحقتماقدعملفيهغيرهاكما.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكلأنهالحقتماقدعملفيهغيرهاكما.claim: With interrogative alif and a wish meaning, ألا governs its complement like ordinary negative لا, dropping nunation and nun just as in the statement form.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكلأنهالحقتماقدعملفيهغيرهاكما.anchor: عملت فيما بعدها فنصبته ولا يحسن لها

SIBAWAYH:وذلكلأنهالحقتماقدعملفيهغيرهاكما.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكلأنهالحقتماقدعملفيهغيرهاكما.speaker: الخليل
SIBAWAYH:وذلكلأنهالحقتماقدعملفيهغيرهاكما.claim: Al-Khalil reads ألا رجلا as a rhetorical prompt, not a wish: roughly ألا تروني رجلا جزاه الله خيرا.

SIBAWAYH:وذلكلأنهالحقتماقدعملفيهغيرهاكما.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكلأنهالحقتماقدعملفيهغيرهاكما.speaker: يونس
SIBAWAYH:وذلكلأنهالحقتماقدعملفيهغيرهاكما.claim: Yūnus explains the tanwīn in ألا رجلا as poetic necessity; Sibawayh says this is a possible analysis, while he presents al-Khalil's prompt reading for others.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكلأنهالحقتماقدعملفيهغيرهاكما.anchor: وأما يونس فزعم أنه نون مضطرا

SIBAWAYH:وذلكلأنهالحقتماقدعملفيهغيرهاكما.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكلأنهالحقتماقدعملفيهغيرهاكما.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكلأنهالحقتماقدعملفيهغيرهاكما.claim: The accusative wish construction is not nominative because it is neither an answer to a question nor a clause meaning ليس.

SIBAWAYH:وذلكلأنهالحقتماقدعملفيهغيرهاكما.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكلأنهالحقتماقدعملفيهغيرهاكما.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكلأنهالحقتماقدعملفيهغيرهاكما.claim: In ألا ماء ولبنا باردا حلوا, the adjectives are nunated because each describes a separate noun: cold water and sweet milk.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكلأنهالحقتماقدعملفيهغيرهاكما.anchor: لا يكون في الصفة إلا التنوين

SIBAWAYH:وذلكلأنهالحقتماقدعملفيهغيرهاكما.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكلأنهالحقتماقدعملفيهغيرهاكما.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكلأنهالحقتماقدعملفيهغيرهاكما.claim: ألا غلام أفضل منك takes the accusative because it is a wish meaning اللهم هب لي غلاما and needs no predicate.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكلأنهالحقتماقدعملفيهغيرهاكما.anchor: إلا بالنصب لأنه دخل فيه معنى التمني

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p833/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p833/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p833/r3.claim: Abraham seeks forgiveness from the Merciful rather than calling on the Compeller, since forgiveness is sought from al-Rahman; he hopes his father may receive mercy and believe.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p833/r3.anchor: وهنا لا يصح أن يقول "سأستغفر لك الجبّار" لأن المغفرة تُطلب من الرحمن وليس من الجبّار

NASHR:v2p319/r12.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p319/r12.speaker: المدنيان وأبو عمرو
NASHR:v2p319/r12.claim: The two Medinans and Abū ʿAmr open the yāʾ in ربي إنه كان.
NASHR:v2p319/r12.anchor: ربي إنه كان فتحها المدنيان، وأبو عمرو

NASHR:v2p319/r13.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p319/r13.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p319/r13.claim: The sūra has no additional yāʾs (yāʾāt al-zawāʾid) in this catalogue.

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p355/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p355/r1.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p355/r1.claim: Al-Zajjaj lists four language senses of salām: the verbal noun of salima, a plural of salāmah, one of God’s names, and a tree.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p355/r1.anchor: قال الزجاج : سمعت محمد بن يزيد يذكر أن السلام في اللغة أربعة أشياء

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p355/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p355/r2.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p355/r2.claim: As a verbal noun, salām is a prayer that a person be safe in religion, self, and property: release from harm.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p355/r2.anchor: قال الزجاج : ومعنى السلام الذي هو مصدر سلمت أنه : دعاء للإنسان أن يسلم من الآفات

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p355/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p355/r3.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p355/r3.claim: As a divine name, al-Salām means the possessor of peace, who owns safety as release from harm.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p355/r3.anchor: والسلام الذي هو اسم الله [ تعالى ] تأويله ذو السلام

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p355/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p355/r4.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p355/r4.claim: The tree called salām is large and strong; the author thinks its name may reflect freedom from afflictions.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p355/r4.anchor: فأما السلام الشجر فهو شجر عظام قوي أحسبه سمي بذلك لسلامته من الآفات

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p355/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p355/r5.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p355/r5.claim: Stones are called salām for their hardness; peace names reconciliation because it means safety from evil, while a ladder carries one where desired.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p355/r5.anchor: وأما السلام : الحجارة فسميت بذلك : لسلامتها من الرخاوة

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p355/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p355/r9.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p355/r9.claim: The fourth sense is goodness; Ibn Qutayba glosses the salām of the Night of Decree as ‘good.’
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p355/r9.anchor: والرابع : الخير . ومنه قوله تعالى [ في هود ]

ITQAN:v2p319/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p319/r6.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p319/r6.claim: Ḥafiyyan means gentle or kind to me.
